claim: The GISAID repository of SARS-CoV-2 genomes currently contains approximately 15 million entries.
source: With currently ≈15 million entries, this unprecedented large database has provided the basis for phylogenetic analyses that have identified critical amino acid mutations associated with immune evasion, infectivity, and disease severity, and allowed the rapid identification of variants of concern (Greaney et al., 2022; Kepler et al., 2021; Obermeyer et al., 2022; Rochman et al., 2021; Viana et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of entries in the GISAID database.

claim: Approximately 86% of N-protein's 419 residues are capable of assuming on average four to five different amino acids without impairment of viability.
source: Besides traditional sequence-based structure prediction and structure/function relationships, and more recent recognition of structural dynamics, new paradigms have emerged with increased understanding of the role of IDRs, their mimicry of SLiMs, nonlocal physicochemical properties of sequence regions, and the ability of IDRs to promote macroscopic phase separation to generate or usurp condensates with virus-related functions. The extensive genomic data of SARS-CoV-2 presents an opportunity to probe how sequence diversity impacts these biophysical properties, and to examine what biophysical constraints exist for viral proteins to support viability. Focusing on SARS-CoV-2 N-protein we have studied the diversity of biophysical phenotypes with the goal to increase understanding of salient mechanisms of the many N-protein functions, and also to glean aspects of the biophysical fitness landscape underlying evolution.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Abstract and refers to previously reported data (Zhao et al., 2022).

claim: The highest frequency of mutations in N-protein occurs in the intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs).
source: The highest frequency of mutations occurs in the substantial IDRs which are the N-arm, linker, and C-arm that flank and connect the folded nucleic acid binding domain (NTD) and the dimerization domain (CTD) (Figure 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation about mutation frequency distribution.

claim: IDRs comprise approximately half of the N-protein molecule.
source: The IDRs comprise approximately half of the molecule and allow large conformational fluctuations (Botova et al., 2024; Cubuk et al., 2021; Redzic et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the proportion of the molecule composed of IDRs.

claim: Approximately 38 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) particles are arranged like beads-on-a-string in the viral particle.
source: It proceeds via nucleic acid (NA) binding-induced conformational changes and oligomerization, leading to the formation of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) particles with as-of-yet unknown molecular architecture, ≈38 of which are arranged like beads-on-a-string in the viral particle (Carlson et al., 2022; Cubuk et al., 2021; Klein et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2021), and are anchored through binding of N-protein to viral M-protein (Lu et al., 2021; Masters, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript states this structural organization with supporting citations.

claim: N-protein is the most abundant viral protein in the infected cell.
source: N-protein is the most abundant viral protein in the infected cell (Finkel et al., 2021), and as we reported previously (Zhao et al., 2022), it is also the most diverse structural protein with approximately 86% of its 419 residues capable of assuming on average four to five different amino acids evidently without impairment of viability.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this with a supporting citation.

claim: N-protein can form macromolecular condensates through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS).
source: N-protein can form macromolecular condensates through LLPS that aid in assembly functions and interactions with host proteins (Carlson et al., 2020; Cascarina and Ross, 2022; Cubuk et al., 2021; Iserman et al., 2020; Jack et al., 2021; Lu et al., 2021; Perdikari et al., 2020; Savastano et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this property with multiple supporting citations.

claim: 5.06 million high-quality SARS-CoV-2 sequences were selected for analysis from data downloaded from Nextstrain in January 2023.
source: SARS-CoV-2 sequence data were downloaded from Nextstrain (Hadfield et al., 2018) in January 2023 and 5.06 million high-quality sequences were selected for analysis.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the dataset used in the study.

claim: The N-protein amino acid sequences exhibit approximately 43 million instances of mutations distributed across approximately 92% of its residues.
source: The N-protein amino acid sequences exhibit ≈43 million instances of mutations distributed across ≈92% of its residues.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these mutation statistics.

claim: Approximately 36% of sequences in the dataset are Delta variant and approximately 49% are Omicron variant sequences.
source: We have previously characterized this dataset with regard to the amino acid mutational landscape of N-protein, and found mutation frequencies that are strongly dependent on position and largely time-invariant, except for the defining mutations arising in variants of concern, the latter comprising ≈36% Delta variant and ≈49% Omicron variant sequences (Schuck and Zhao, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the proportions of variants in the dataset.

claim: Sequence plasticity is highest in the IDRs, with an average of 5.2 different possible amino acid mutations at each residue compared to 2.9 different mutations on average in the folded domains.
source: It may be discerned that sequence plasticity is highest in the IDRs, with an average of 5.2 different possible amino acid mutations at each residue compared to 2.9 different mutations on average in the folded domains.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these statistics and refers to Figure 1B showing the histogram of mutations.

claim: 6300 distinct full-length N-protein sequences were identified, each represented in at least 10 different genomes in the database.
source: For a robust analysis, each mutated sequence was required to be represented in at least 10 different genomes in the database. This led to 6300 distinct full-length N-protein sequences (N-FL; 1–419).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the filtering criteria and resulting number of sequences.

claim: Hydrophobicity is uniformly high and polarity correspondingly low in the folded NTD and CTD domains.
source: Focusing on folded N-protein modules, we find that hydrophobicity is uniformly high and polarity correspondingly low in the folded NTD and CTD domains, which is consistent with the expectation that folded structures are stabilized by buried hydrophobic residues (Eisenberg and McLachlan, 1986; Kauzmann, 1959).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data and provides theoretical justification with citations.

claim: The N-arm and C-arm are the most polar regions of N-protein.
source: In particular, the N-arm and C-arm are most polar: despite a very large dispersion across the mutant spectrum, their values do not overlap with those of the folded domains.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data.

claim: The SR-rich region exhibits high polarity and low hydrophobicity, while the L-rich region exhibits opposite behavior.
source: It is useful to subdivide the linker IDR further to distinguish the SR-rich region (N:175–205), which exhibits high polarity and low hydrophobicity, from the L-rich region (N:206–247), which exhibits opposite behavior and is among the sequence stretches with lowest polarity values and highest hydrophobicity (Figure 2, red arrows in magenta shaded columns).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes these contrasting properties observed in Figure 2.

claim: The SR-rich region provides a major hub for phosphorylation, aids in NA binding, and mediates NA binding-induced allosteric interactions between NTD and the L-rich region.
source: Indeed, these regions in the linker IDR have been recognized to play distinct functional roles: The SR-rich region provides a major hub for phosphorylation, aids in NA binding, and mediates NA binding-induced allosteric interactions between NTD and the L-rich region (Pontoriero et al., 2022; Yaron et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these functional roles with supporting citations.

claim: The L-rich region has a propensity for the formation of transient helices that interact with NSP3.
source: This is distinct from the L-rich region, which has a propensity for the formation of transient helices that interact with NSP3 (Bessa et al., 2022), and can assemble via hydrophobic interactions to form coiled-coil oligomers that contribute to the architecture of RNPs in viral assembly (Adly et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this property with supporting citations.

claim: The L-rich region can assemble via hydrophobic interactions to form coiled-coil oligomers that contribute to the architecture of RNPs in viral assembly.
source: This is distinct from the L-rich region, which has a propensity for the formation of transient helices that interact with NSP3 (Bessa et al., 2022), and can assemble via hydrophobic interactions to form coiled-coil oligomers that contribute to the architecture of RNPs in viral assembly (Adly et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this assembly property with supporting citations.

claim: The C-arm1 region is the most polar region of the entire N-protein.
source: Similarly, the C-arm IDR can be subdivided into the N3 region (N:390–419) and the remainder ('C-arm1', N:364–389), which also have strikingly different properties (Figure 2, blue arrows in cyan shaded columns): Whereas the connecting C-arm portion is by far the most polar, the N-terminal N3 region is among the most hydrophobic regions of the entire protein.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data.

claim: The N3 region is among the most hydrophobic regions of the entire N-protein.
source: Similarly, the C-arm IDR can be subdivided into the N3 region (N:390–419) and the remainder ('C-arm1', N:364–389), which also have strikingly different properties (Figure 2, blue arrows in cyan shaded columns): Whereas the connecting C-arm portion is by far the most polar, the N-terminal N3 region is among the most hydrophobic regions of the entire protein.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data.

claim: The N3 region contains a transient helix.
source: Interestingly, the N3 region contains a transient helix (Cubuk et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2022), which may be involved in recognition of the packaging signal and M-protein interactions localized here (Kuo et al., 2016; Masters, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this structural feature with supporting citations.

claim: Viable N-protein sequences can have significant spread of net charges among all the mutants, amounting to departures by ±(1–2) from the ancestral sequence.
source: Similar to polarity and hydrophobicity, viable sequences can have significant spread of net charges among all the mutants, amounting to departures by ±(1–2) from the ancestral sequence.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 3A data.

claim: The L-rich sequence is nearly neutral in charge despite the strongly basic character of the linker.
source: However, noteworthy is again the contrast arising from subdivision of the linker and C-arm, which displays uneven and non-overlapping distributions: despite the strongly basic character of the linker, its L-rich sequence is nearly neutral; similarly, the basic C-arm splits into an even more basic C-arm1 and an acidic N3 tail region.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 3A data.

claim: The N3 tail region is acidic.
source: However, noteworthy is again the contrast arising from subdivision of the linker and C-arm, which displays uneven and non-overlapping distributions: despite the strongly basic character of the linker, its L-rich sequence is nearly neutral; similarly, the basic C-arm splits into an even more basic C-arm1 and an acidic N3 tail region.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 3A data.

claim: Most serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues in the disordered regions (30 of 37) have been found phosphorylated in different proteomic analyses.
source: As reviewed in Yaron et al., 2022, most serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues in the disordered regions (30 of 37) have been found phosphorylated in different proteomic analyses.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with a citation to a review.

claim: Maximal phosphorylation of all serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues in the IDRs leads to a negative charge for all IDRs.
source: Accordingly, we estimated the maximum charge when all of these residues in the IDRs are phosphorylated (Figure 3B). This leads to a negative charge for all IDRs.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this calculated result shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The largest impact of phosphorylation was found in the SR-rich region of the linker, which carries the highest density of phosphorylation sites.
source: As might be expected, the largest impact was found in the SR-rich region of the linker, which carries the highest density of phosphorylation sites.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 3B data.

claim: The defining mutations of the Delta and Omicron variants impact the hydrophobicity, polarity, and charges in all of the N-protein regions.
source: It is noteworthy that the defining mutations of the Delta and Omicron variant (denoted by dotted red and dashed green horizontal lines, respectively) do impact the hydrophobicity, polarity, and charges in all of the N-protein regions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The values of physicochemical properties for Delta and Omicron variants do not stand out from the clouds of values across the mutant spectrum.
source: However, their values do not stand out from the clouds of values across the mutant spectrum, which include more extreme values throughout.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Related coronaviruses present high sequence identity scores for the full-length protein and the folded domains, but little to no sequence identity in the IDRs (with exception of SARS-CoV-1).
source: As shown in Table 1, the resulting peptides present high sequence identity scores for the FL protein and the folded domains, but, with exception of SARS-CoV-1, have little to no sequence identity in the IDRs.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Table 1 data.

claim: The pattern of hydrophobicity and polarity values of IDRs relative to those of the folded domains is closely mirrored for SARS-CoV-1, MERS, and MHV.
source: Nonetheless, the pattern observed for SARS-CoV-2 of hydrophobicity and polarity values of IDRs relative to those of the folded domains, and the pattern comparing subdivisions of the IDRs is closely mirrored for SARS-CoV-1, MERS, and MHV (red symbols).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data.

claim: All coronavirus linker peptides have higher polarity than their corresponding full-length, NTD, or CTD regions.
source: Polarity values (Figure 2A) of all coronavirus linker peptides are higher than either their corresponding FL, NTD, or CTD regions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2A data.

claim: The subdivision of the linker in the peptides corresponding to SR-rich and L-rich regions of SARS-CoV-2 follow the same qualitative trend for all coronaviruses studied.
source: The subdivision of the linker in the peptides corresponding to SR-rich and L-rich regions of SARS-CoV-2 follow the same qualitative trend, with higher polarity in the equivalent SR-rich and lower polarity in the equivalent L-rich peptides for all coronaviruses studied.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 2 data.

claim: The charge properties and phosphorylation of the equivalent IDR sub-regions are functional biophysical constraints maintained across related coronaviruses despite little sequence conservation.
source: This suggests that the charge properties and phosphorylation, like polarity and hydrophobicity, of the equivalent IDR sub-regions are functional biophysical constraints maintained across related coronaviruses despite little sequence conservation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the comparative analysis.

claim: N:D63G exhibits a shift in intrinsic fluorescence quantum yield compared to Nref.
source: The presence of the N:D63G mutation in the NTD is highlighted in the shift of the intrinsic fluorescence quantum yield of this mutant in comparison to Nref (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The shift in fluorescence quantum yield for N:D63G may be attributed to changes in the local environment of tryptophan W108.
source: This may be attributed to changes in the local environment of tryptophan W108, which is partially surface exposed and structurally near the aspartic acid D63, as indicated by AlphaFold structural predictions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation based on structural predictions.

claim: No significant differences in the intrinsic binding affinity to T10 was detected between N:D63G, other mutants, and the ancestral species.
source: No significant differences in the intrinsic binding affinity to T10 was detected between N:D63G, other mutants, and the ancestral species (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this experimental result shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: A major transition in differential scanning fluorometry is observed with an inflection point at Ti ≈ 49°C for N-protein.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, a major transition is observed with an inflection point at Ti ≈ 49°C.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 4B data.

claim: Omicron mutations No, N:R203K/G204R, and N:P13L/Δ31–33 are neutral with respect to thermal stability.
source: Compared to the reproducibility of transition temperatures of ±0.3°C, significant shifts from the ancestral N-protein can be discerned: While Omicron mutations No, N:R203K/G204R, and N:P13L/Δ31–33 are neutral, those occurring in the Delta variant (N:D63G, N:G215C, and Nδ) are destabilizing, i.e., they lower the transition temperature.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 4B data.

claim: Delta variant mutations (N:D63G, N:G215C, and Nδ) are destabilizing and lower the transition temperature.
source: Compared to the reproducibility of transition temperatures of ±0.3°C, significant shifts from the ancestral N-protein can be discerned: While Omicron mutations No, N:R203K/G204R, and N:P13L/Δ31–33 are neutral, those occurring in the Delta variant (N:D63G, N:G215C, and Nδ) are destabilizing, i.e., they lower the transition temperature.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 4B data.

claim: Apparent destabilization of the folded domains occurs in N:G215C despite the absence of mutations in the folded domains.
source: Interestingly, apparent destabilization of the folded domains occurs in N:G215C despite the absence of mutations in the folded domains – 215C being located in the middle of the linker IDR.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 4B data.

claim: The nonlocal mutation effect of N:G215C points to altered intra-molecular interactions between IDRs and the folded domains, and/or changes in contacts between folded domains mediated through an altered oligomeric state.
source: This nonlocal mutation effect points to altered intra-molecular interactions between IDRs and the folded domains, and/or changes in contacts between folded domains mediated through an altered oligomeric state.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the N:G215C data.

claim: Significantly less disorder and greater helicity is observed for N:G215C compared to the ancestral Nref.
source: Compared to the ancestral Nref, significantly less disorder and greater helicity is observed for N:G215C (and to lesser extent also for Nδ), whereas slightly more disorder is indicated for N:R203K/G204R.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 4C data.

claim: For N:G215C, increased helicity can be attributed to the stabilization of transient helices in the leucine-rich region of the central linker IDR.
source: For N:G215C, increased helicity can be attributed to the stabilization of transient helices in the leucine-rich region of the central linker IDR, as shown previously (Zhao et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation with supporting citations.

claim: The ancestral N-protein at micromolar concentrations in NA-free form is a tightly linked dimer sedimenting at approximately 4 S, without significant populations of higher oligomers.
source: As reported previously, the ancestral N-protein at micromolar concentrations in NA-free form is a tightly linked dimer sedimenting at ≈4 S, without significant populations of higher oligomers (Forsythe et al., 2021; Ribeiro-Filho et al., 2022; Tarczewska et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this property with supporting citations.

claim: N:D63G, No, N:R203K/G204R, and N:P13L/Δ31–33 exhibit the same dimeric behavior as Nref at low micromolar concentrations.
source: The same behavior is observed for N:D63G, No, N:R203K/G204R, as well as N:P13L/Δ31–33 at low micromolar concentrations (Figure 5A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5A data.

claim: The G215C mutation promotes the formation of higher oligomers via stabilization of coiled-coil interactions of transient helices in the L-rich linker region.
source: By contrast, the G215C mutation promotes the formation of higher oligomers via stabilization of coiled-coil interactions of transient helices in the L-rich linker region (Zhao et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation with supporting citations.

claim: Oligomerization beyond the dimeric Nref is also observed for Nδ, but less than for N:G215C.
source: Oligomerization beyond the dimeric Nref is also observed for Nδ, which incorporates the 215C mutation, but less than for N:G215C.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5A data.

claim: Nref forms clusters and particles at temperatures greater than 55°C.
source: As reported previously, Nref forms clusters and particles at >55°C (Zhao et al., 2021), which is strongly enhanced and occurs at a lower temperature for N:G215C, due to the enhancement of the linker oligomerization (Figure 5B; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation with supporting citations.

claim: Particle formation is strongly enhanced and occurs at a lower temperature for N:G215C due to the enhancement of the linker oligomerization.
source: As reported previously, Nref forms clusters and particles at >55°C (Zhao et al., 2021), which is strongly enhanced and occurs at a lower temperature for N:G215C, due to the enhancement of the linker oligomerization (Figure 5B; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation with supporting citations.

claim: N:D63G shows an onset of particle formation at approximately 50°C and larger particle averages than the ancestral protein.
source: More moderate enhancement of particle formation is observed for N:D63G, which shows an onset already at ≈50°C and larger particle averages than the ancestral protein.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5B data.

claim: Strong inhibition of particle formation is observed for the N:R203K/G204R double mutant.
source: The opposite effect, strong inhibition of particle formation, is observed for the N:R203K/G204R double mutant.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5B data.

claim: N:R203K/G204R forms particles only at temperatures greater than 70°C, as a mixture of smaller clusters with some very large aggregates.
source: Here, particles form only at temperatures >70°C, as a mixture of smaller clusters with some very large aggregates that adventitiously enter the light path in DLS and cause fluctuations in the z-average Stokes radius.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5B data.

claim: No exhibits slightly enhanced particle formation relative to the ancestral Nref, comparable to N:D63G.
source: Interestingly, although No comprises the R203K/G204R mutation, No does not share this behavior but instead exhibit slightly enhanced particle formation relative to the ancestral Nref, comparable to N:D63G.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 5B data.

claim: Solutions of N:P13L/Δ31–33(1–43) exhibited elevated viscosity after storage for several days at 4°C.
source: Unexpectedly, solutions of N:P13L/Δ31–33(1–43) exhibited elevated viscosity after storage for several days at 4°C in 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.5.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this experimental observation.

claim: ColabFold predicts that replacement of proline at position 13 by leucine allows for formation of parallel sheets symmetrically arranged in higher-order N-arm oligomers.
source: Even though ColabFold is trained to predict folded structures, it has been found to be frequently successful in predicting transient folds in IDRs (Alderson et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2023). Indeed, it predicts that replacement of proline at position 13 by leucine allows for formation of parallel sheets symmetrically arranged in higher-order N-arm oligomers (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this prediction result shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reference N-arm Nref:(1–43) and the construct carrying the Δ31–33 deletion behave as expected for non-interacting peptides.
source: While the reference N-arm Nref:(1–43) and the construct carrying the Δ31–33 deletion behave as expected for non-interacting peptides of this size, the N-arm constructs carrying the P13L mutation (in particular, the Omicron N-arm N:P13L/Δ31–33(1–43)) exhibit very large correlation times.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 6A data.

claim: The N-arm constructs carrying the P13L mutation exhibit very large correlation times in DLS.
source: While the reference N-arm Nref:(1–43) and the construct carrying the Δ31–33 deletion behave as expected for non-interacting peptides of this size, the N-arm constructs carrying the P13L mutation (in particular, the Omicron N-arm N:P13L/Δ31–33(1–43)) exhibit very large correlation times.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 6A data.

claim: Rapidly sedimenting, anomalously shaped boundaries with approximately 100-fold larger sedimentation coefficient were observed for the Omicron N-arm and the construct carrying solely the P13L mutation in SV-AUC.
source: Similarly, in SV-AUC (Figure 6B) the ancestral reference and the Δ31–33 deletion mutant sediment as expected for non-interacting N-arm peptides (Zhao et al., 2023), whereas rapidly sedimenting, anomalously shaped boundaries with ≈100-fold larger sedimentation coefficient were observed for the Omicron N-arm and the construct carrying solely the P13L mutation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 6B data.

claim: The P13L mutation introduces new protein self-association interfaces in the N-arm.
source: This unequivocally demonstrates the introduction of new protein self-association interfaces from the P13L mutation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Nref readily forms droplets in the presence of T40 oligonucleotides.
source: As may be discerned from the top left panel of Figure 7, Nref readily forms droplets in the presence of T40 oligonucleotides.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 7.

claim: N:R203K/G204R does not display droplets under the same conditions as Nref, but forms few large particles with fibrillar morphology.
source: Under the same conditions, N:R203K/G204R (bottom left) does not display droplets, but forms few large particles with fibrillar morphology.

source: In stark contrast, N:P13L/Δ31–33 (bottom center) readily forms droplets that appear to be more rapidly merging and growing than those of Nref (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).

source: The most polydisperse distribution with largest droplets were observed for N:G215C (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Viable N-protein sequences can have significant variation of physicochemical properties within the mutant spectrum.
source: On one hand, our studies of the diversity of nonlocal physicochemical properties of N-protein revealed the absence of tightly controlled hydrophobicity, polarity, and charges outside the folded domains. In the IDRs, individual mutations may alter each of these properties apparently without impacting viability, although modulatory fitness effects may be possible.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion from the computational analysis.

claim: A very clear separation of physicochemical parameters far exceeding mutational dispersion is maintained between the L-rich and SR-rich region of the linker IDR, and between the N3 and remaining region of the C-arm IDR.
source: On the other hand, a very clear separation of physicochemical parameters far exceeding mutational dispersion is maintained between the L-rich and SR-rich region of the linker IDR, and between the N3 and remaining region of the C-arm IDR.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion from the computational analysis.

claim: Point mutations in N-protein can affect protein properties on all levels of organization, from thermodynamic stability and secondary structure to intra- and inter-molecular interactions, oligomeric state, particle formation, and LLPS.
source: Strikingly, point mutations can affect protein properties on all levels of organization, from thermodynamic stability and secondary structure to intra- and inter-molecular interactions, oligomeric state, particle formation, and LLPS.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: Mutations can impact the transient helix in the hydrophobic L-rich region of the linker, and promote its helical conformation and self-association into higher oligomeric states.
source: First, mutations can impact the transient helix in the hydrophobic L-rich region of the linker, and, as we have shown previously, promote its helical conformation and self-association into higher oligomeric states (Zhao et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: Introduction of N:G215C in a reverse genetics system resulted in enhanced viral replication and larger virions.
source: Notably, introduction of N:G215C in a reverse genetics system resulted in enhanced viral replication and larger virions (Kubinski et al., 2024).

source: In the present study, we found that full-length N:R203K/G204R strongly opposes both temperature-driven particle formation and LLPS with oligonucleotides.

evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with a supporting citation.

source: It is interesting to note that the R203K/G204R mutation, the P13L mutation, and the P13L/Δ31–33 combination each can occur independently of each other in viable virus species, with 261 genomes in the database carrying only the P13L mutation, 9548 only the combination P13L/Δ31–33, and >50,000 genomes exclusively the double mutation R203K/G204R, even though their more frequent coexistence (by approximately 10-fold, in all of Omicron variants) might suggest epistatic interactions and a fitness advantage.

claim: 9548 genomes carry only the combination P13L/Δ31–33.
source: It is interesting to note that the R203K/G204R mutation, the P13L mutation, and the P13L/Δ31–33 combination each can occur independently of each other in viable virus species, with 261 genomes in the database carrying only the P13L mutation, 9548 only the combination P13L/Δ31–33, and >50,000 genomes exclusively the double mutation R203K/G204R, even though their more frequent coexistence (by approximately 10-fold, in all of Omicron variants) might suggest epistatic interactions and a fitness advantage.
